# TikTok Ad Hooks: 40 Ready-to-Film Openers That Earn the Next Three Seconds

Someone sees your TikTok ad, flicks a thumb, and it is gone before your product has a chance. The fix is not a longer explanation. It is a first line that tells the right person, fast, why this video concerns them. Below are 40 TikTok ad hooks you can film today, with a spoken line, the text to put on screen, and a hook type you can test.

![Three Hook Lab hooks for one video](https://uploads.postiz.com/hIHxrr41KT.png)

Keep any result you claim honest. When a line needs a figure, replace `[ADD: your number]` with a number you can support. If you do not have one, use a problem, question, or callout instead.

## Fitness and wellness offers

For offers aimed at people who want to start, restart, or keep a simple routine.

   On-screen: "Day 1 is where you quit"  
   Type: Contrarian
2. Spoken: "Why does everyone quit by January 20th?"  
   On-screen: "The January 20th wall"  
   Type: Question
3. Spoken: "You're not lazy. You're doing week one wrong."  
   On-screen: "Week 1 mistake"  
   Type: Mistake
4. Spoken: "If workouts keep falling off your calendar, start here."  
   On-screen: "For people who cannot stay consistent"  
   Type: Callout
5. Spoken: "This is the 10-minute workout I use on busy days."  
   On-screen: "10 minutes still counts"  
   Type: Result
6. Spoken: "Your plan is too hard if it fails on a Tuesday."  
   On-screen: "Make your plan Tuesday-proof"  
   Type: Contrarian
7. Spoken: "I trained for [ADD: your number] weeks without starting over."  
   On-screen: "No restart Monday"  
   Type: Result
8. Spoken: "Beginners, do this before buying another supplement."  
   On-screen: "Start here, not in the supplement aisle"  
   Type: Callout

## How to choose and test TikTok ad hooks

Pick a hook that your ad can actually pay off. A question needs an answer in the video. A result needs proof. A callout needs a clear audience. If the opening promises a fix, show the fix before the viewer feels tricked into staying.

Say each spoken line out loud. If it takes longer than about three seconds, cut the throat-clearing words. The on-screen line should also make sense with sound off, but it does not have to repeat the spoken line word for word.

For a clean test, keep the body of the ad the same and record two or three different openings. Post or run them under comparable conditions. Then compare the first moments of retention, watch time, clicks, and the action you actually want. Write down the hook type that earns attention from your audience. One winning version is useful; a pattern across several tests is better.

## FAQ

### How long should a TikTok ad hook be?

Aim for one spoken sentence that fits in roughly three seconds. If a viewer needs to reread the screen text, shorten that too.

### Should the spoken line and on-screen text match?

They should support the same promise. Let the spoken line carry the voice and let the text give a quick, readable version for people watching muted.

### Can I use a result hook without a number?

Yes, if you can show a real outcome. Do not invent a figure to make the line sound stronger. Use `[ADD: your number]` only after you have a number you can verify.

### What should I test first?

Use the same ad body with a contrarian line, a callout, and a question. That isolates the opening and gives you a useful first comparison.

Here is a shortened, published example of the response format:

**You send:** "Hooks for a 30s TikTok about why most people quit the gym in January — energetic, for beginners."

**You get back (shortened):**

- **Caption:** short caption + CTA + hashtags, plus one filming tip.
